current_revision.mathematical_scope: Given an initial smooth marked family relative to a protected set K, the free reductions and actual region/component incidence, rel-K critical-area realization is equivalent to a positive matrix with the prescribed free row demands and component masses. Smooth positive selection, fixed-support componentwise primitives and Moser give a smooth relative family even if protected masses themselves are not smooth. Strict cuts and componentwise total equalities characterize feasibility. Actual P0 source annuli yield a connected incidence graph and sufficiently small zero-total smooth area changes, preserving full nodal neighborhoods, canonical moment, circle action, end germs and whole-fiber overlaps. This does not reach arbitrary prescribed atlas targets. Separately, finite anchor-period conditions imply K4/Petersen charts on the existing actual Liouville filling; critical actions scale homogeneously, and comparison with neck lines retains residual primitive constants and integer shear. The anchor Stokes total formula assumes actual Euler clutching. Irrational slopes obstruct a chart of that fixed filling. Large-target feasibility, actual framing transport and simultaneous two-end/open-collar matching remain inputs before the existing GH replacement theorem applies. General transport, Moser, action-angle, cone-extension and GH principles are not claimed as new.
